nodes.summary: Appends an arc (a straight line to its start, then round a centre) to a FollowPath waypoint string.
what: Starts radius from (cx, cy) at start_angle, turns sweep rad (+ = counterclockwise seen from above) and ends at end_radius: a spiral if the two differ.
approach=false drops the straight line, so the arc starts from the previous point.
With pan the arc is cut into an even number of pieces of at most pan_step rad, and the heading swings +pan, −pan, +pan… along it: a camera sweep.

nodes.summary: Appends one waypoint, with its heading options, to a FollowPath waypoint string.
what: Writes path + "frame: x,y,z,yaw | options;" to out. Leave path empty to start a new path.
A non-zero roll or pitch writes six numbers. Options are written only when set: heading, look_at, yaw_offset, spin, spin_rate, yaw_frame.
FAILURE if heading is not waypoint, path or look_at, or if look_frame is given with a heading other than look_at.

ports.name: num_cycles
ports.desc: Number of full counterclockwise turns

ports.name: yaw_rate
ports.desc: Target ramp speed in radians/second; unset: as fast as the controller follows
ports.default: unset: as fast as the controller follows

ports.name: timeout_secs
ports.desc: Overall timeout; default 90 seconds

ports.name: odom_timeout_secs
ports.desc: Odometry watchdog; default 1 second

nodes.summary: Spins whole counterclockwise turns in place, counting the real, unwrapped yaw from odometry.
what: Holds the position of the first odometry message and ramps a level yaw target. Without yaw_rate the target stays at most 0.6 rad ahead of the measured yaw, so it turns as fast as the controller follows.
SUCCESS within 0.05 rad of the full rotation, with yaw rate under 0.05 rad/s and roll and pitch under 0.1 rad.
FAILURE after timeout_secs or a gap in odometry longer than odom_timeout_secs; it then holds the current heading.

ports.name: frame
ports.desc: Frame of waypoints without their own (default world)

ports.name: waypoints
ports.desc: "x,y,z,yaw; frame: x,y,z,yaw | arc=cx,cy,sweep; ..." (or x,y,z,roll,pitch,yaw); {blackboard} references allowed

ports.name: min_depth
ports.desc: Shallowest allowed z in world (default -0.55)

ports.name: max_depth
ports.desc: Deepest allowed z in world (default -4)

ports.name: timeout
ports.desc: Seconds before giving up (default 60)

ports.name: spin_rate
ports.desc: Steady spin for the whole path, rad per metre (about rad/s / cruise speed; default 0)

ports.name: max_speed
ports.desc: Cruise speed cap for this path, m/s (default 0: the controller's own limit)

nodes.summary: Flies a list of waypoints with the MPC's follow_path action: through each one without stopping, settling only on the last.
what: Parses waypoints when it starts: "x,y,z,yaw; frame: x,y,z,yaw | option=value; ..." (6 numbers adds roll and pitch). {key} entries are filled from the blackboard first.
Waits up to 3 s for every waypoint's frame in TF, then sends one goal. Each point stays in its own frame, so a path through mapping's object frames moves when they move.

Depth is clamped in world to [max_depth, min_depth]. SUCCESS when the goal succeeds; FAILURE if it is rejected, aborted or takes longer than timeout (the goal is then cancelled, as it is when the node is halted).
watch: Any message on controller/linear or controller/angular ends a running path: the MPC treats it as a new setpoint (finishPath in mpc_controller_node.cpp).

nodes.summary: Sends one ControllerCommand: a position (or velocity) setpoint on controller/linear, or an attitude on controller/angular.
what: isOrientation picks the topic. In POSITION mode (mode 3) an orientation's x, y, z are roll, pitch, yaw, sent as a quaternion.
SUCCESS at once: it does not wait for Talos to get there. The older move subtrees (PrimitiveMovePosition) poll GetOdometry to see when it has.
watch: It also ends any FollowPath that is running.

nodes.summary: Sets the controller parameter controller__stunt__safe_mode through a parameter client.
what: At load it looks for a node named like /complete_controller, else one ending in /mpc_controller.
RUNNING until the parameter is set; FAILURE after timeout_secs.
watch: The MPC does not declare this parameter, so it always fails on Talos today: the Nereus run in this chapter logged "parameter 'controller__stunt__safe_mode' cannot be set because it was not declared" and timed out 10 s later. In the competition tree it runs in FlipTree at the gate, just after a DISABLED setpoint, so the controller is off for those 10 s. Its failure ends the flip, which a ForceSuccess wraps.

nodes.summary: Publishes a stunt state on controller/stunt_state (a UInt16), for the old controller's flip.
what: Publishes targetStuntState once and returns SUCCESS straight away.
Its retry loop (republish every 2 s, fail after 5 tries, watching controller/running_stunt_state) is in onRunning, which never runs because onStart already succeeded.
watch: Nothing in the current workspace or in Nereus subscribes to controller/stunt_state; it belonged to the old controller. In the competition tree's FlipTree it never runs: SetControllerSafeMode fails before it.

nodes.summary: Starts mapping's binary classifier, which splits one detector class into two numbered objects.
what: Calls a riptide_msgs2/StartBinaryClassifier service with class_name, object1_name and object2_name. SUCCESS if the response says success. Same timing rules as CallTriggerService.

ports.name: object_name
ports.desc: Detector class to center

ports.name: min_score
ports.desc: Ignore weaker detections; default 0.2

ports.name: max_age_secs
ports.desc: Lost once no detection is this old; default 1.5

ports.name: timeout_secs
ports.desc: Give up after; default 8

ports.name: yaw_tolerance
ports.desc: Centered within this (rad); default 0.05

ports.name: depth_tolerance
ports.desc: Level within this (m); default 0.1

ports.name: center_depth
ports.desc: false: yaw only; default true

ports.name: min_depth
ports.desc: Shallowest depth to move to; default -0.75

ports.name: max_depth

ports.name: base_frame
ports.desc: Vehicle frame; default talos/base_link

ports.name: align_yaw
ports.desc: Move square on to the object (its frame's yaw); false: turn in place; default true

ports.name: object_frame
ports.desc: Frame whose yaw to align with; default <object_name>_frame

ports.name: standoff
ports.desc: Camera distance in front of it (m); default the range it was seen from
ports.default: the range it was seen from

ports.name: position_tolerance
ports.desc: There within this (m); default 0.1

ports.name: align_tolerance
ports.desc: Square on within this (rad); default 0.08

nodes.summary: Chases a detection with the forward camera: yaws to keep it centred and moves square on in front of the object.
what: Yaws so the detection sits on the camera's axis (allowing for the camera's offset from the centre of Talos) and changes depth until the camera is level with the object.
With align_yaw it also moves onto the object's front (the +x side of object_frame) at standoff, facing it square on.

Detection positions are smoothed (each new one moves the estimate 30 % of the way). SUCCESS once centred, level and in place; FAILURE if the object is lost for max_age_secs or after timeout_secs, when it stops where it is.

nodes.summary: Waits for the next estimate of one object and outputs its error, a single number for how well it is known.
what: Subscribes to mapping/<Target> when it starts and waits for one message (FAILURE after 5 s).
Covariance is not a distance: the square root of the summed squared variances, the three angular ones divided by 2π (see How Talos sees, Chapter 9).

nodes.summary: Reads mapping's current target and lock from state/mapping.
what: Waits for the next state/mapping message after it starts and writes map_locked and target_name. FAILURE after 3 s (outputs false and empty).

ports.name: object_name
ports.desc: Detector class

ports.name: frame
ports.desc: Frame for the output position; default world

ports.name: max_age_secs
ports.desc: Fail if the latest detection is older; default 1.0

ports.name: min_score
ports.desc: Ignore weaker detections; default 0.2

nodes.summary: Where the detector last saw an object, in a chosen frame (default world).
what: Keeps the strongest detection of each class from every detected_objects message, and transforms it through TF at the detection's own timestamp, so a turning vehicle doesn't smear it.
SUCCESS with out_x/y/z if that detection is at most max_age_secs old and scores at least min_score; otherwise FAILURE.
Lets the down-camera search aim at what it actually sees, before mapping has moved the object's frame.

ports.name: object
ports.desc: Mapping object (mapping/<object>), or a comma list that must all converge

ports.name: target_cov
ports.desc: Converged below this error (getCovariance's)

nodes.summary: A condition: SUCCESS once every object in a comma list has an error below target_cov.
what: Answers at once, so it can sit in a ReactiveSequence and stop a running search the moment the estimate is good enough.
Only trusts estimates received since it started being ticked (a gap of more than 1 s, or a new object list, starts a new check), so an estimate from before a SetMappingTarget reset can't pass it.
Subscribes to each mapping/<object> the first time it is ticked with that name.

nodes.summary: A condition: SUCCESS if the detector saw the object within the last max_age_secs.
what: Counts any detection at or above min_score on detected_objects, and any object mapping reports on mapping/fused (so bin_target1, which the detector never names, counts too).
Answers at once: in a ReactiveSequence it interrupts a running move as soon as the object comes into view.

nodes.summary: Tells mapping which objects to fuse (the target) and whether to lock the map.
what: Calls the mapping_target service with target_object (one name or a comma list; empty for none) and lock_map.
FAILURE if the service isn't there within 1 s or doesn't answer within time_limit_secs; otherwise SUCCESS (the response is empty).

nodes.summary: Waits until the detector reports object_name, or fails after timeout_secs.
what: Checks only each detection's first result (results[0]) and ignores the score. The competition tree uses SeenRecently instead.

nodes.summary: Where talos/base_link must go so that a tool frame (a camera, the claw, a torpedo tube) sits at a given pose relative to a target frame.
what: Looks up base → link and reference → world in TF and computes the base pose in world (formula in the chapter).
Outputs out_x … out_oy in world; FAILURE if the frames aren't in TF within 5 s.

nodes.summary: Reads roll, pitch and yaw from a sensor_msgs/Imu topic.
what: Subscribes to topic when it starts and waits up to 3 s for one message.

nodes.summary: Writes the vehicle's current pose from odometry/filtered to the blackboard.
what: Waits for a fresh message after it starts (FAILURE after 3 s) and writes x, y, z and roll, pitch, yaw (rad).
watch: Its subscription is made when the tree is loaded, so every one of its {n} instances in the competition tree receives every odometry message for the whole run.

ports.name: topic
ports.desc: Topic to listen to

nodes.summary: Reads one geometry_msgs/Twist message into six outputs.
what: Subscribes to topic when it starts; FAILURE after 3 s. The competition tree reads the MPC's settle trust, controller/scale/trust, with it.

ports.name: timeout_secs
ports.desc: Reset and odometry confirmation timeout (default 5 seconds)

ports.name: position_tolerance
ports.desc: Reset confirmation tolerance in meters (default 0.1)

ports.name: orientation_tolerance
ports.desc: Reset confirmation tolerance in radians (default 0.1)

nodes.summary: Resets the EKF's pose with robot_localization's set_pose service, then waits until odometry shows it.
what: Fields not chosen with setX, setY, setZ, setOrientation are copied from the latest odometry.
After the service answers, waits for an odometry message newer than the request that lies within position_tolerance and orientation_tolerance. FAILURE after timeout_secs.

nodes.summary: Re-expresses a pose (x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw) given in from_frame in to_frame.
what: Uses the latest transform in TF. Retries every tick and fails if the transform isn't there within 3 s.

nodes.summary: Calls any std_srvs/SetBool service with data; SUCCESS if it answers success.
what: Same timing as CallTriggerService. Logs the response's message as a warning.
The competition tree arms the actuators (command/actuator/arm) and switches the detector between cameras (set_camera_is_dfc: true = down camera) with it.

nodes.summary: Calls any riptide_msgs2/SetString service with data; SUCCESS if it answers success.
what: Same timing as CallTriggerService. Used for mapping's background targets, the bin geometry fit and the slalom type.

nodes.summary: Calls any std_srvs/Trigger service; SUCCESS if it answers success.
what: FAILURE if the service isn't there within 1 s, answers success = false, or takes longer than time_limit_secs.

The competition tree fires the torpedo and dropper with it (command/actuator/torpedo, command/actuator/dropper, served by actuator_service_translator.py) and calls mapping's classifier and table services.

nodes.summary: Reads the actuator board's state: claw, torpedoes, droppers and whether it is busy.
what: Needs one message on both state/actuator/status and state/actuator/busy after it starts; FAILURE after 3 s. States are the numbers in riptide_msgs2/ActuatorStatus (torpedo 3 = charged, dropper 2 = ready…).

nodes.summary: Reads one std_msgs/Bool from any topic into the blackboard.
what: Subscribes when it starts and waits for the next message; after 3 s it writes false and fails. The competition tree reads the kill switch (state/kill) with it while waiting to start.

nodes.summary: Reads one std_msgs/Float64 from any topic into the blackboard.
what: Subscribes when it starts and waits for the next message; after 3 s it writes 0 and fails.

nodes.summary: Publishes one std_msgs/Float32 on any topic.
what: Creates the publisher when it starts and publishes once; SUCCESS. The competition tree publishes claw moves with it on command/actuator/claw_move_s, which Nereus's claw answers. No firmware in titan_firmware listens to that topic (the actuator board takes command/actuator/claw), so check it before relying on it in the pool.

nodes.summary: Publishes one integer on any topic. Despite the name, the message is a std_msgs/UInt16.
what: Creates the publisher when it starts and publishes once; SUCCESS. Only used for controller/stunt_state.

nodes.summary: SUCCESS if its input is non-empty: a quick "has this blackboard key been set?"
what: An unset key reads as empty, so input="{key}" fails until something writes the key.

nodes.summary: A decorator: ticks its child again and again until it succeeds, or fails once num_seconds have passed.
what: A failed child is retried on the next tick (every 30 ms), not straight away, and the decorator reports RUNNING meanwhile.
FAILURE (with an error in the log) when the time is up.
watch: When it times out it does not halt a child that is still RUNNING (read from the code; not yet tested in Nereus). A FollowPath inside skips its onHalted, so the MPC keeps flying that path until the next setpoint or path.

nodes.summary: RUNNING for the given number of seconds, then SUCCESS.
what: Uses the ROS clock, so in Nereus it waits in simulated time.

nodes.summary: A condition: |a − b| < range.
what: Answers at once. Only one tree file uses it, outside the competition tree.

nodes.summary: A condition: angles a and b (rad) within range of each other.
what: Wraps a − b before comparing, so a = 3.1, b = −3.1 counts as close; swapped, it doesn't (see Watch).
watch: Only differences above +π are wrapped. One below −π is not: a = −3.1, b = 3.1 fails a 0.25 rad check although the angles are 0.08 rad apart. The competition tree uses it once per attitude check in PrimitiveMoveOrientation (range 0.25).

nodes.summary: Straight-line 3D distance between (x1, y1, z1) and (x2, y2, z2).
what: Always SUCCESS.

nodes.summary: A condition: a > b, a < b or a == b, chosen by test.
what: Any other test logs an error and fails.

nodes.summary: Fills {key} entries in a string from the blackboard: "{object_name}_frame" becomes "torpedo_frame".
what: A {key} that isn't on the blackboard is left as it is. Always SUCCESS.

nodes.summary: The yaw (rad) that faces from (currX, currY) to (targX, targY): atan2(Δy, Δx).
what: Always SUCCESS.

nodes.summary: A condition: SUCCESS if value reads as true.
what: The value goes through BT.CPP's string-to-bool conversion, so "1" and "true" both work.

nodes.summary: out = a operator b, for + − * /.
what: Always SUCCESS. An unknown operator gives 0; dividing by 0 is not caught.

nodes.summary: Logs a message at ERROR level, with {key} entries filled from the blackboard.
what: Always SUCCESS: logging an error does not fail the tree. To fail, wrap a log line in ForceFailure, as AssertTree does.

what: Always SUCCESS. Lines appear in doTask's log, under the node name autonomy.

nodes.summary: Sets the LED strips to a named status pattern on command/led.
what: Publishes one LedCommand to all strips and returns SUCCESS. An unknown name logs a warning and shows undefined (solid white).
